intro: Israel is a parliamentary democracy with no written constitution, governed instead by a set of Basic Laws.

chapters.title: How it works
text: Voters elect the 120-member Knesset by proportional representation, so governments are always coalitions. The prime minister leads the government, and the president is a ceremonial head of state.
Israel considers Jerusalem its capital, but most countries keep their embassies in Tel Aviv because the city's status is disputed.

chapters.title: Big debates
text: In 2023 plans to limit the power of the Supreme Court led to some of the largest protests in Israel's history. The future of the occupied territories and Israeli settlements remains the biggest question.
